title: Rast pits on lap one and wins at Zandvoort
dek: René Rast won Race 2 at Zandvoort from third on the grid for Audi's first win of 2018, 0.824 seconds ahead of pole-sitter Gary Paffett, after stopping at the end of lap one.

chapters.title: Mercedes ahead, Rast with a score to settle
text: Saturday had belonged to Mercedes. Gary Paffett won Race 1 from pole in front of Paul di Resta, Lucas Auer and Pascal Wehrlein, and a safety car had undone René Rast's long first stint and dropped him to 17th. Paffett left Zandvoort's first race with 127 points to Di Resta's 106, with Timo Glock third on 100 and Marco Wittmann fourth on 98.
Race 2 on Sunday 15 July was the last start before the summer break, and with the mandatory pit stop again part of the race, strategy was the obvious way to reshuffle the Saturday order.

chapters.title: Paffett's first lap is enough for pole
text: Paffett put the session out of reach with his very first flying lap, a 1:30.225 that was 0.446 seconds quicker than Philipp Eng's BMW. He could not improve on the second runs, but nobody got close. Rast was third on 1:30.716, 0.491 off the pole time, so the top three on the grid held an Audi, a BMW and a Mercedes.

Wehrlein set his best time early, then braked too late for the first corner and went through the gravel, spreading sand over the racing line. He qualified fourth, with Di Resta fifth, Mike Rockenfeller sixth and Bruno Spengler seventh. Wittmann was 12th, and Glock, the best BMW on Saturday, started 17th.

Joel Eriksson crashed in the morning practice and his BMW was repaired only just in time for him to set a lap with minutes to spare, which put him 14th. Robin Frijns, the home favourite, had lost the morning practice session with an electrical problem on his Audi, made a single run and started last.

chapters.title: Rast stops at the end of lap one
text: Paffett kept the lead off the start, with Eng second and Rast third. Further back, Glock almost stalled and had to work through the field from the rear. Rast then did the opposite of what he had done on Saturday: he dived into the pits at the end of the first lap for his mandatory stop, accepting that his second set of tyres would have to last almost the whole distance, in return for clear track.

Eng held second place through the early laps with Wehrlein and Di Resta behind him. Paffett came in at the end of lap ten and the stop was not quick, so Rast was ahead of him when the Mercedes rejoined. Wehrlein ran deep into the race on his first set of tyres before making his own stop.

chapters.title: Green hits Spengler and the field bunches up
text: On lap 21 Jamie Green ran into Spengler's BMW at the first corner and pushed it into the gravel, and as Spengler could not get out of the gravel on his own, the safety car came out. Green was given a drive-through penalty for the incident. The later stoppers had only just been in, so the order at the front stayed as it was: Rast led Paffett and Di Resta for the restart.
The restart was again in double file, and Rast held his lead from Paffett. Further back there was contact between Loïc Duval and Wittmann, and both cars were damaged.

chapters.title: Rast holds Paffett off by 0.824 seconds
text: For most of the final stint Rast kept the gap to Paffett at just over half a second. Paffett, on the fresher tyres, trimmed it to 0.4 seconds with three laps left, but could not find a way past on a circuit where passing is hard, and Rast pulled away again to cross the line 0.824 seconds ahead after 35 laps in 56:44.864.

Di Resta was third, 1.349 seconds behind, and Eng finished fourth, 1.825 behind, ahead of Augusto Farfus, who was fifth, 2.123 behind. Wehrlein took sixth, followed by Nico Müller, Edoardo Mortara, Auer and Glock, who climbed from 17th to tenth. Wittmann dropped to 17th, over a minute behind, and Frijns retired after ten laps. Rockenfeller set the fastest lap, a 1:31.805 on lap 32, despite finishing 16th.

chapters.title: Paffett 27 clear at the break
text: Rast called the win a release after a long dry spell and several hard weeks, in which he had often had good pace without the result. He said the team had chosen a very aggressive strategy again after Saturday, and that the safety car had made the end of the race tense. Paffett, who had been second, said Rast had earned it after his bad luck on Saturday, and that the early stop had been a risk with tyre wear that Rast managed very well.

For Paffett the weekend still added up to what he called nearly perfect: two poles, a win and a second place, and 49 points from the two races. Di Resta said he could be happy with two podiums, that he had lost a little ground at the top, and that at the halfway stage consistency would pay off in the end.
Paffett went into the break with 148 points, 27 ahead of Di Resta on 121. Rast's win more than doubled his tally to 49 points and made him the best-placed Audi driver.

Mercedes could look back on a weekend of two poles, a win and five podium places. Team principal Ulrich Fritz had called Saturday's four-car result a remarkable performance on such a demanding track, and the Sunday double podium kept Paffett and Di Resta first and second in the standings. Audi, by contrast, had broken its winless run at the halfway point of the season with its reigning champion, and had finished the weekend with Rast as its top driver in the table.

BMW's weekend had been quieter. Eng, the best BMW in fourth, missed the podium by under half a second, Farfus was fifth, and Glock recovered from a bad start to finish tenth. Wittmann, fourth in the standings, ended Race 2 in 17th after the restart damage, while Frijns followed his fifth place and best-Audi finish on Saturday with a retirement at his home race.
The championship resumed at Brands Hatch on 11 and 12 August, which Paffett described as his home race.

facts.v: Rast won from third on the grid for Audi's first DTM victory of the season, after pitting at the end of lap one.
